besluite.fout: 'hulle reg bly staan' leaves the singular 'reg' without a clear referent.
besluite.rede: 'daarop' ties the right to the food and house just named; the right still stands unconditionally and nobody new is made responsible.

besluite.fout: 'die land ... hy' is informal personification; written Afrikaans refers to a country with 'dit'.
besluite.rede: Pronoun and possessive fix only; the country still carries the duty and the double negative is intact.
'kos om van te groei' follows the normal Afrikaans pattern of 'geld om van te lewe', so the change is lateral, and 'sodat hy kan groei' could be read as linking to the right rather than to the food.
'iemand sonder sorg laat' is complete, natural Afrikaans; 'los' is only a more colloquial alternative.
'die reën en die koue keer' is idiomatic, while 'kan uithou' reads first as 'can withstand', which moves the meaning away from keeping the rain and cold out.

besluite.fout: After 'nie ... spot nie', the elided 'en jou hande was' can make a reader stumble over whether the negative carries across.
besluite.rede: Repeating 'dat jy' removes the stumble and matches the previous sentence's pattern without changing what is asked.

This sentence must keep its exact meaning; 'dit' points at the responsibilities just listed, and 'nie altyd alles regkry nie' widens it to getting everything right and shifts the scope of the negation.

besluite.fout: 'geboortedag' usually reads as 'birthday', but a certificate shows the full date of birth.
besluite.rede: The point is real, but this is a glossary definition shared across lessons, so only the writer may change its wording.
